## 1 · How to read the tool's output

```
 no   section              label                       paper      code     diff   verdict
 14   table2               Clinic · train              0.706      0.706   0.0000  PASS
338   delong_Table 4       test2 vs Clinic             0.336      0.371   0.0351  DISCREPANCY
680   table_s15            n complete cases            377        374     3.0000  DISCREPANCY
```

Run with `-v` to print the PASS rows as well, and `--section table2` to check a
single table.  The exit status is non-zero only when a genuine, *undocumented*
`FAIL` remains — which is never, in the current state.  A `DISCREPANCY` is a
published number that disagrees with the data; each one is registered in
`src/hrpca/gold.py` (`KNOWN_DISCREPANCIES` and `KNOWN_SECTION_DISCREPANCIES`)
together with the corrected value and the reason.

## 2 · The conventions that the numbers depend on

Every one of these was a live trap in the archive; all are fixed in code.

### 2.1 Statistical conventions

| # | Convention | What goes wrong otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Training-cohort AUCs use the 16-significant-digit export** (`data/scores_highprec.csv`) | the released training scores are rounded to two decimals; the clinical AUC becomes 0.704 instead of 0.706 and the all-habitat AUC 0.863 instead of 0.864 |
| 2 | **The combined model's training AUC uses the deployed scores** (`data/scores/train.csv`) | the `Combined` column of the historical 16-digit export is a **superseded model** and gives 0.795 instead of 0.798 |
| 3 | **mean \|SHAP\| uses the full 398-patient training cohort as the reference** | the 391-row subset used to draw the SHAP panel gives 0.561 for H4 instead of 0.565 |
| 4 | **Hosmer–Lemeshow uses `pandas.qcut` equal-frequency bins with `df = bins − 2`** | hand-rolled equal-width bins give 0.210 instead of 0.351 for the training cohort |
| 5 | **The combined model is linear in probabilities, not log-odds** | the closed-form SHAP attribution `βᵢ(xᵢ − E[xᵢ])` and the published coefficients only hold on the probability scale |
| 6 | **Cox recalibration is fitted within each cohort** | the pooled-external intercept/slope (−0.513 / 1.239) require pooling the three external cohorts before fitting |
| 7 | **IDI is `Δ(mean p \| event − mean p \| non-event)` on the probability scale** | the log-odds variant gives 0.72 instead of 0.124 for the training cohort |

### 2.2 Data conventions — **the cross-table key**

`Clinic.csv` (numeric ID), `label.csv` (`.nii.gz` names) and the score files
(a within-cohort row index) share **no** key.  The authoritative link is
`data/cases_with_ids.csv`:

```
derived_data/<cohort>_scores_label.csv
      │ (patient_index)          ← the eight score columns are byte-identical
      ▼
cases_with_ids.csv  ──(real_id)──►  Clinic.csv
                    ──(real_id)──►  label.csv
                    ──(real_id)──►  heatmap_data_all.csv / model_inputs.csv
```

| # | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | **Never pair rows by position.** | the files use different sort orders (`heatmap_data_all` is sorted by `Combined` ascending); positional Pearson is **0.00–0.08**, while joining on ID gives 339/339 identical rows in test cohort 1 |
| 9 | **For the training cohort use `heatmap_data_all.csv` as the ID source.** | `cases_with_ids.csv`'s `real_id` is verified correct for the three external cohorts (Pearson 1.0000) but only 1/398 for training |
| 10 | **`heatmap_data_all.csv`'s `habitat` / `H1` / `H3` / `H5` columns are a different model** from the deployed scores (same AUC, 0/398 identical rows).  Only `Clinic` / `H2` / `H4` agree with `model_inputs_all.csv`. | use `data/scores/*.csv` for the signature scores |

## 3 · The 17 discrepancies, in detail

### 3.1 Table 4 / Table S5 — DeLong (11 cells)

The recomputed values agree with the pipeline's own exports
(`derived_data/*_Delong.csv`) to six decimals in **16 of 16** comparable cells.
Table 4 and Table S5 disagree with the pipeline **and with each other**:

| Comparison | Table 4 | Table S5 | Pipeline export | Recomputed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| test 2, combined vs clinical | 0.336 | 0.345 | **0.3711** | **0.3711** |
| test 1, combined vs clinical | 0.255 | 0.092 | **0.2553** | **0.2553** |
| prospective, combined vs clinical | 0.003 | <.001 | **0.0031** | **0.0031** |
| prospective, combined vs H2 | 0.066 | 0.089 | **0.0664** | **0.0664** |
| training, combined vs H4 | 0.012 | 0.015 | **0.0124** | **0.0119** |
| prospective, combined vs H4 | 0.202 | 0.198 | **0.2016** | **0.2016** |
| prospective, combined vs all-habitat | 0.003 | 0.005 | **0.0029** | **0.0029** |
| test 2, combined vs H2 | 0.002 | 0.003 | **0.0013** | **0.0013** |
| pooled external, combined vs clinical | 0.025 | 0.006 | — | **0.0218** |

**Verdict: Table 4 is wrong in 2 cells (test 2 vs clinical; pooled vs clinical);
Table S5 is wrong in 9.**  The correct values are the pipeline's own
`*_Delong.csv` exports.  The pooled value 0.0218 is corroborated three times in
the manuscript (Table S10 .022; Table S16b P = .022), so Table 4's .025 and
Table S5's .006 are both transcription variants; Table S12b's `Combined vs
Clinical` row (P .025) repeats Table 4 and should also read .022.

### 3.2 Table S15 — regression (5 cells)

| Cell | Published | Recomputed | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| n complete cases | 377 | **374** | the missing-data pattern *matches the paper's footnote exactly* (7 training patients lack ISUP, 14 lack PSA), so the convention is right and the clinical table differs by version |
| PI-RADS, multivariable OR | 1.611 (1.048–2.477) | **1.565 (1.015–2.413)** | the only substantive estimate that moves |
| PSA density, univariable OR | 1.118 (1.031–1.212) | 1.123 (1.031–1.221) | last digit |
| PSA density, multivariable CI upper | 1.117 | 1.122 | last digit |

**The other five univariable odds ratios and the multivariable ISUP estimate
reproduce exactly** (ISUP 2.047 / 1.890, PI-RADS 1.681, PSA 1.006, Age 1.003,
target-ROI volume 0.995, prostate volume 0.996).

**Note on the cohort**: Table S15 was fitted on the **full screening table**
(`labels.csv`, n = 1125), not on the frozen 1016-patient analysis set.  On the
analysis set the univariable ISUP odds ratio is 2.059; on the full table it is
2.047, which is what the paper prints.  The verifier therefore uses the full
table.

### 3.3 Table 1 — one cell

With the correct join (`heatmap_data_all.csv` ←→ `Clinic.csv` on the numeric ID):

* **all 12 PI-RADS cells reproduce exactly** (37/88/273, 75/107/157, 47/62/80,
  6/23/61), and so do all four cohort sizes;
* **15 of the 16 ISUP cells reproduce exactly**;
* the exception is **ISUP grade group 3 in the training cohort: 76 published vs
  83 in the data**.  The published ISUP counts sum to **391** for a cohort of
  398 — the seven patients without an ISUP grade group appear to have been
  folded into grade 3.  If that is the intent the published count should be 83
  (21%); the table footnote already discloses the 7 missing values;
* the continuous medians agree to 0.1–1.6 units (largest: prospective
  target-ROI volume Q3, 29.4 vs 30.99 mL); the P values are of the same
  magnitude (Age .045 vs .038, PSA <.001 vs <1e-4, volumes .007 vs .0055 and
  .005 vs .0065).

Corrected values: `results/tables/discrepancy_table1_recomputed.csv`.

### 3.4 Two smaller cells

| Cell | Published | Recomputed | Explanation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Table S10, training ΔAUC | +0.092 | **+0.0942** | the difference of the table's own two rounded AUCs (0.798 − 0.706) is 0.092; the unrounded difference is 0.0942 |
| Table 2, ResNet-18 T2WI test cohort 1 | 0.557 | **0.556** | `derived_data/dl_comparator_results.csv` stores 0.556500, which rounds to 0.557; the comparator CSV supplied with the submission stores 0.556 |

### 3.5 Table S9 — mixed provenance, not a habitat-row error

The **`Combined` row of Table S9 reproduces exactly** under the deployed-score
convention (0.3514 / 0.0002 / 0.0177 / 0.0729 against 0.351 / 0.0002 / 0.018 /
0.073), and so does Table S17a.

The **habitat rows (Habitat, H1–H5) are equal, cell by cell, to the archived
`derived_data/hosmer_all.csv`** — the pipeline's Hosmer–Lemeshow output on its
*own* modelling matrix, not on the deployed scores:

| Signature | Cohort | Published | `hosmer_all.csv` | Recomputed on deployed scores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Habitat | Training | 0.052 | **0.0517** | 0.6502 |
| Habitat | Test 1 | 0.089 | **0.0886** | 0.0000 |
| Habitat | Test 2 | 0.208 | **0.2080** | 0.0000 |
| Habitat | Prospective | 0.830 | **0.8303** | 0.0013 |
| H1 | Test 1 | 0.003 | **0.0026** | 0.0000 |
| H1 | Test 2 | 0.974 | **0.9741** | 0.0000 |
| H2 | Test 1 | 0.314 | **0.3142** | 0.0000 |
| H3 | Test 2 | 0.828 | **0.8283** | 0.0004 |
| H4 | Test 2 | 0.115 | **0.1150** | 0.0000 |
| H5 | Test 2 | 0.687 | **0.6870** | 0.0000 |

All 20 habitat cells match `hosmer_all.csv` to ≤ 0.0008.  The **`Clinic` row
matches neither source** (published .012 / .0004 / .091 / .380; deployed scores
.034 / .0007 / .035 / .116; pipeline export .066 / .0003 / .047 / .375).

**Consequence**: Table S9 mixes two sources in one table.  The table note
already states that the habitat values come "from the analysis pipeline", so the
habitat rows are internally consistent with their stated provenance (they are
the reason the verifier reports them as SKIP rather than DISCREPANCY); what is
missing is that the **`Combined` row comes from the deployed scores** and that
the **`Clinic` row matches neither**.  Recommended fix: `FINAL_VALUES.md` §二.

### 3.6 Table S16a — no discrepancy

With the correct join the deployed clinical score reproduces the published row
**exactly** (0.7064 / 0.7952 / 0.7697 / 0.6890 → 0.706 / 0.795 / 0.770 / 0.689).
A fresh ISUP + PI-RADS logistic fit on the released covariates differs slightly
(0.702 / 0.804 / 0.771 / 0.680) only because the deployed score came from the
pipeline's own modelling matrix; on the test cohorts the two are
**rank-identical** (Pearson 1.0000, maximum absolute difference 0.0031).  The
deployed fit is `logit(p) = −4.9697 + 0.6561·ISUP + 0.3298·PI-RADS`.

## 4 · The 99 SKIPs, and why each is unavoidable

| Group | n | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Table S9 habitat-signature H-L values | 20 | they are reproducible from `hosmer_all.csv` but **not** from the deployed scores; choosing the convention is an editorial decision, see §3.5 |
| Table S13 "clinical avoided / missed" columns | 30 | the archived comparator does not reproduce these numbers (see below) |
| Table S21 subgroups and interaction P values | 17 | subgroup membership needs the patient identifier, which the score files do not carry |
| Table S18 — corrected-case sensitivity analysis | 9 | same reason: the 52-case correction list cannot be joined to the score files |
| Table S16b comparator AUCs | 2 | the archived WTR comparator run gives 0.791 for the training cohort, where Table S6a prints 0.790; the matched-comparison scoring files are not in the release |
| mean \|SHAP\| on the 391-row subset; Table S16a refit rows | 15 | reported for information only; conventions 3 and 9 apply |
| Table S19 three-sequence row; Wilcoxon P values; Table S2 note | 6 | the 100 per-fold AUCs and the three-sequence comparator row are not in the release |

**Table S13's comparator columns.** The combined-model columns of Table S13
(`eplnd`, `avoided`, `missed`, net benefit) reproduce **exactly — all 30 values,
in all four cohorts**; the recomputed "avoided" count is the number of pN0
patients above the threshold (300 of 536 at the 15% threshold, exactly as
published).  The "clinical model (avoided / missed)" column does not follow from
the released clinical scores: at the 15% threshold in the training cohort the
published pair is 74 / 10 while the released clinical score gives 206 / 10, and
in test cohort 1 the published pair is 126 / 5 against 168 / 5.  The *pooled
external* values in that column are close to the recomputed ones, so the column
appears to mix cohorts.

## 5 · Items the verifier cannot test at all (no imaging data)

These steps are implemented and documented but cannot be executed from the
release, because they need the DICOM/NIfTI images, the masks or the trained
network:

| Item | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dice 0.95 against manual delineation (n = 30) | Methods 2.3, Table S8 | implementation provided (`src/01_segmentation.py --check`) |
| Calinski–Harabasz K = 2, silhouette, Davies–Bouldin by K | Table S3c | implementation provided (`src/02_habitat_clustering.py --criteria`) |
| 1,197 candidate features after region remapping | Table S8 | `src/03_feature_extraction.py --candidates`; the shipped habitat tables give 1,197 columns per habitat |
| The 27-feature LASSO fit | Table S14 | the **retained feature list and its statistics reproduce exactly** (87/87, §0); re-running LASSO on the shipped habitat tables does **not** return the same 27 features — see finding F8 |
| Habitat purity / fragmentation, null model, tiny-habitat rates | Table S3d, S4, Fig. S1/S5 | implementation provided; needs the voxel partitions |
| Table S1 scanner inventory | Table S1 | scanner census scripts are archived; needs the DICOM headers |

### Finding F8 — the 27-feature model is not reproducible from the habitat tables

Refitting an unpenalised logistic regression on the 27 retained features taken
from `data/features/rad_features_h*.csv` gives a **training AUC of 0.745–0.756**,
not 0.864; the archived coefficient file (`_habitat27_coef.csv`, 27 coefficients
+ intercept) applied to those same columns gives **0.700**.  Neither reproduces
Table 2's 0.864.  The frozen per-patient score in `data/scores/` **does** give
0.864 and is the value the paper reports.  Conclusion: the habitat feature tables
that were delivered are not the matrix on which the reported model was fitted,
most likely because they were re-extracted after the production run.  All 87
Table S14 values (feature names, habitats, RF importance, mean \|SHAP\|) *are*
reproduced from `SHAP_k5_feature_stats.csv`, so the retained set itself is
consistent.

## 6 · What a reader of this repository should do

1. Read [`FINAL_VALUES.md`](FINAL_VALUES.md) — it is the cell-by-cell list with
   the corrected value and a recommendation for each of the 17 discrepancies.
2. Run `python verify/check_paper_numbers.py -v` and inspect the **DISCREPANCY**
   rows; each carries the corrected value in its `note` column.
3. Where a discrepancy is a **reporting** issue (the 11 DeLong cells, the ΔAUC
   of +0.092, the T2WI 0.557/0.556), correcting the manuscript text is enough.
4. Where it is a **data/version** issue (Table S15, the Table 1 ISUP cell), the
   table has to be regenerated; the corrected values produced by this repository
   are in `results/tables/`:
   * `discrepancy1_delong_final.csv` — the DeLong three-source comparison
   * `discrepancy3_tableS15_grid.csv` — the Table S15 candidate grid
   * `discrepancy_table1_recomputed.csv` — Table 1 with the correct join
   * `tableS9_hosmer.csv` — Table S9 under the deployed-score convention
   * `table2_auc_ci.csv`, `table3_habitat_number.csv`, `table4_delong.csv`
   * `tableS12a_robustness.csv`, `tableS12b_pairwise.csv`
   * `tableS17a_recalibration.csv`, `tableS13_dca_clinical_terms.csv`,
     `tableS17b_decision_impact.csv`, `tableS17c_net_benefit.csv`
   * `tableS2a_habitat_profiles.csv`, `tableS2b_habitat_zscores.csv`
   * `tableS3_k_selection.csv`, `figS9_mean_abs_shap.csv`, `shap_per_patient.csv`
